## Active

### D-901 — Port the service by identifier, and drop the machinery a declared name makes pointless

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

T-707 ported the service to declared identifiers, and four choices were made on the way that the
code alone does not explain. The ledger class is SignalLedger in service/ledger.ts, not a renamed
TemplateRegistry in service/registry.ts: the package already has a registry.ts for the declared
vocabulary, and two files called registry in one package is the kind of ambiguity that costs a
reader a minute every time. The entry field is ref and its value is the identifier itself, so every
downstream consumer the port kept (the diagram, the flow ledger, the search) still speaks of a
record's ref while the reference is greppable back to the declaration that produced it.

The snapshot was reset to version 1 and no longer names an embedding provider. semantic-log needed
the provider identity because its vectors were only comparable within one provider at one width;
with the vectors gone that check has nothing to compare, so the third fault kind went with it rather
than remaining as a rule kept for its own sake. A version 99 file is still quarantined as
unsupported and a file that parses but is not a ledger is still corrupt.

The ingest lost its per-event skip path. semantic-log separated a malformed batch from an event
whose embedding failed, because the emitter is fire-and-forget and one unusable event must not
discard the good ones beside it. With the embedding gone there is no per-event work left that can
fail, so a batch is accepted or rejected whole and the skipped count and its onSkipped hook were
removed instead of remaining as a number that can only ever be zero. A dependency that throws now
rejects the batch, which is honest: nothing about the event's data caused it.

The sink is typed IServiceRecord extends LogRecord with signal added, not against the emitter's
summary record. A Writer is handed the full record, with its refs, its flow position and its
progress marks, and the emitter summary carries none of those. T-710 is where the emitter starts
filling signal on every record it writes; until then a caller that wants its records counted
forwards them with the field set, and the sink refuses a record without one rather than putting an
entry on the ledger keyed by nothing.

One field was widened rather than worked around: FlowState.kind is optional on a record. The ambient
identity a call inherits may name a flow execution and no kind, and the ledger already treats a
kindless flow as an execution whose steps are retained but which contributes to no per-kind union.
Requiring the field forced either a fabricated kind or a flow the type could not express.

### D-910 — The legacy work order is a source census, not a run-time list

> _2026-11-19 · core/lukaot · active_

The inventory of unswept level calls is taken over the source, not over a run, even though `T-704`'s
compatibility logger exists to give such a call an identity at run time. A runtime list is what the
design wants eventually, but it has two properties that make it the wrong thing to hand a sweeper
today: it only names calls that executed, so a branch no test reaches is invisible, and the
framework does not yet route level calls through the compatibility logger at all, so the list would
be empty while 37 calls remain.

A source census says what is left, is cheap, and shrinks visibly as the work lands — one line per
package, the sites behind it on request, and `check` for the day it should be zero. What it counts
is `log?.<level>?.(…)`: a component writing a line, which is exactly what a sweep removes. It does
not count fastify's own logger (`request.log`, `fastify.log`, `app.log`) or the pino-shaped
`log.logger(level, …)` the loader hands to fastify, because neither is a caller's line and an entry
for one would be a task nobody can complete.

When the compatibility logger is wired into the framework's level face — a decision nobody has taken
— the two descriptions should agree, and this command stays worth keeping: it is the one that counts
what never ran.

### D-912 — The lukaot root stays importable in a page; the logger and store move to ./node

> _2026-11-19 · core/lukaot · active_

The kukum e2e proved what a comment had only asserted: shared framework code is bundled for a page
out of the same tree as the server, so a browser build of `Gateway` follows `@feasibleone/lukaot`
into whatever that entry exports. Three edges cost the page its whole module chain —
`node:async_hooks` through the ambient store, and `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, `node:os`, `node:path`
through the logger, its fingerprint and the store beside it — and a static import into a node
builtin does not fail on use: a bundler rewrites it into a module whose named exports throw when the
module graph is _linked_, so no `try`/`catch` at the call site can save it.

Two shapes were possible: make every node-bound module reach the builtin without a static import, or
let the root be platform-free and put those modules behind a subpath. The first was rejected as the
general answer — it makes every module responsible for its own degradation, and a filesystem is not
something a page can degrade to — but it is the right answer for exactly one case, the ambient
store, because the browser genuinely needs identity and capability and genuinely cannot have
`AsyncLocalStorage`: `context.ts` reads the class through `process.getBuiltinModule` and keeps a
flat one-frame store where there is no `process`, so `withCapability` still nests correctly in a
page and simply does not survive an `await` there.

For the rest, the root is platform-free and `@feasibleone/lukaot/node` re-exports it whole beside
the logger, the store and the fingerprint: three consumers had to change (`LukaotLog.ts` and one
test), and `src/package.test.ts` now pins both halves — the root carries no logger and `/node` does.
The rule that follows is the one to keep: a module in this package's root graph may not import a
`node:` builtin, and `legacy`-style proof is the browser bundle, not a review.

### D-913 — The rewording fault is gone: a message is a declaration now

> _2026-11-19 · core/lukaot · active_

The flow fixtures carried five faults, and one of them stopped existing when the calls became
declarations: F3 reworded the hub's liquidity message as a deploy would, so a reader could see that
a record's identity did not move when its sentence did. A message is now the declaration's, not the
call site's — the record carries the identifier, and the sentence is interpolated from the
declaration — so there is nothing left at a call site for a fault flag to reword. Keeping the fault
would have meant writing two declarations for one event and a switch between them, which would have
taught the opposite of what the conversion is for.

So F3 is removed rather than reimplemented, and the property it demonstrated is asserted
structurally instead: `src/package.test.ts` pins which half of the package carries what, and the
artifact test compares rendered diagrams whose labels are identifiers. A reworded message is now a
diff in a vocabulary file, which is the review a message should get.

### D-914 — A decision is declared, and declaring it never changes control flow

> _2026-11-19 · core/lukaot · active_

A decision's discriminator was the last literal in a call site that everything else has already
given up: signals, errors and captures are declared, and `decide('route-selection', …)` sat beside
them as a string nobody could search for, count, or check. So `declare()` gained a fourth kind —
`decision` — with the arms it offers and a sentence for each, and `decide()` takes the declaration
instead of the name.

What that buys, concretely: the discriminator on a record is the declared identifier, so it greps
the same way a signal does and the diagram's `alt` label is a name rather than a phrase; the arms
are a closed set, so an arm the declaration does not offer is a compile error at the call site
instead of an arrow nothing can select; and the sentence that explains an arm lives beside it rather
than in a docs page that drifts from the code.

Three things it deliberately does not do. It does not count: a count needs a registry, `decide` has
none, and the service already counts what arrives — the rationale is in the record, so the ledger
can group by discriminator and arm without a second store in the process. It does not fail at
runtime over a mismatch: a decision never changes control flow, so an arm the code names and the
declaration does not is recorded as it ran and the compiler is the only gate. And it does not make a
declaration mandatory — `decide('some-name', …)` still works, because a caller that has not declared
its decisions is not broken by the kind existing, and a library cannot force its host to declare.

`enabled: false` on a decision is the one configuration knob, and it is the shape the property
needs: the branch still runs and only the recording stops, which is what a hot path wants and what a
control flow must never depend on.

### D-930 — The record sink ships in lukaot, not in the viewer

> _2026-11-20 · core/lukaot · active_

The sink that ships records to a collector lives in `@feasibleone/lukaot/node`, beside the writer
contract and the record shape, and the batch wire format lives beside it. It was in
`tools/blong-log`, which forced every consumer to name a viewer package it does not depend on: the
configuration had to spell out `@feasibleone/blong-log/writer`, and nothing in this repository can
resolve that name because no package depends on the tool.

So `log.destination` reads an address as the common case — `{host, port}` or `udp://host:port` — and
builds the shipped sink with no package name at all. A module is still named when a process wants a
destination the framework does not ship: `{module, options}` or a bare string. The batch header is
exported from the same place the sink imports it, so a collector reads the definition that writes it
and cannot drift.

It is **added** to what the process already writes, through `createFanoutWriter`, never substituted
for it. Installing it as the only writer silenced the process: a run configured with a destination
printed nothing on its own terminal, and the spawn test that waits for "nothing to run" hung for its
full two minutes instead of failing. The lesson generalises: a log destination is a place records
also go, and anything that replaces the console makes the process harder to debug than no
destination at all.

The viewer keeps only what reads records: the server, the buffer, the components. `blong-log` no
longer exports a writer, and the pino transport that is still there for other pino users imports the
batch format from lukaot.

### D-940 — A record that names a flow is attributable without a signal

> _2026-11-20 · core/lukaot · active_

A record reaches the service when it can be attributed, and there are two ways to be: naming a
declared signal, or belonging to a flow. The second is the ordinary case a served request is made of

- the realm logs, the runtime dispatches, the port answers, all inside the flow the route minted,
  and none of those records reaches a declaration - so the sink refusing a record without a signal
  shipped nothing for a successful request. Every flow page, every execution row and every diagram
  are drawn from what arrives here, so the symptom was an empty page rather than a missing count:
  three realms' Playwright specs expect the page's own read to appear as an execution named after
  its method.

So the rule is narrower than the one @@D-889 implies. A flow is an identity the ledger already
indexes (executions, unions, lineage), which makes the record placeable without inventing a key for
the signal index; the signal index is the register of what was declared, and a fabricated entry
there would put a value in a filter no source contains. What stays refused is a record that names
neither, and that is what the transport and the ingest now check.

The ingest's placement follows: an accepted event with no signal is reported to the accepted-event
seam (lineage and flow ledger) and counted against nothing, so a batch can be accepted whole without
every event having a ledger entry. The alternative - synthesize a signal from the message template

- was rejected twice over: it is the fingerprint identity @@D-889 deliberately replaced, and it
  would fill the signal filter with hashes.

The same regression had a second half, in the emitter: the call channel wrote its records through
the level API at debug, so a process configured at info produced none at all. Whether a flow records
calls is the calls capability, not the level threshold - @@D-223 says so and says there is no
fallback if they stop being produced - so the channel now binds its own logger at debug and the
write path skips the terminal for a call record unless log.calls.stdout asks for it.

### D-878 — The declared identifier is the signal's identity, and it carries no punctuation

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

Identity is one camelCase token — `agentTicketNotFound`, `agentTicketSkipped` — so the declaration
key, the call site, the policy override, the counter and the reference are the same string, and one
search finds every one of them without quoting. It reads as the semantic triple (subject, object,
predicate) the rest of the framework is named with, and a dotted form is derived by `methodParts`
only where a view wants a namespace. Alternative rejected: a dotted key, which needs quotes at every
site and gives one signal two spellings.

### D-879 — An error signal records when it is created, and throwing is the caller's statement

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

`throw errors.agentTicketNotFound({ticketId})` is one call because construction is the record; the
gateway's existing handling of `ITypedError` is untouched. `silent: true` declares control flow — a
nested early exit — that records nothing by default, which is the shape typed errors already had.
Alternative rejected: a `throw` that reaches the logger, which cannot be detected without wrapping
caller code.

### D-880 — A vocabulary may be declared imperatively; a signal is never emitted imperatively

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

Some names are only known at assembly time — a library computing its keys, a handler group declaring
inline — so `declare()` may be called from code as well as from a layer file. What the prompt does
not allow is an imperative _call_: lukaot has no level API, the level is a policy rather than an
argument, and every emission is a method of a declared vocabulary (`signal?.x?.(…)`). Consequence:
`log?.(…)` disappears from the tree rather than being given a compatibility identity, which is also
why no message-derived identity survives anywhere.

### D-881 — The call site is captured at property access, file only by default

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

Destructuring the vocabulary through the proxy is the one moment the source is known, so a `get`
trap records `{file, line, function}` and the dependency edge before the call happens.
`captureStack: false` keeps it to the file (and line when the frame reports one), which the owner
chose as sufficient; a full stack is opt-in for a session that is debugging. Capture is skipped for
a disabled signal, so the cost follows what is switched on.

### D-886 — A disabled log signal is absent from the proxy

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

Optional chaining is the

discipline the prompt asks for, and it only skips work if the member can be `undefined`: a log
signal below threshold, disabled by configuration or sampled out resolves to `undefined`, so
`signal?.x?.({…})` never assembles the record it would not emit. An error signal is never absent —
it has to return the value the caller throws — so policy can silence its record but never its
construction.

### D-887 — Policy is an in-process registry, patched by configuration and hot reload

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

Declared defaults, then a namespace override (`agent` covers every signal whose identifier begins
with it) and an exact one (`agentTicketSkipped`), then a runtime patch; the effective policy is read
at call time. A database-backed store is deferred with a recorded todo, because it needs a schema
per database and a load path that the in-process registry does not.

### D-888 — The cluster service keeps declared identity, the flow ledger, diagrams and search

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

Identity is now a name, so the registry is a counter table keyed by method name; the flow ledger and
the diagrams are ported unchanged in shape. The embedding provider, centroid geometry, drift and
incident correlation are dropped: with identity declared, novelty and rate become counts on a name,
and the geometry was the weakest-evidenced part of v1.

### D-897 — `pino` leaves the framework and becomes lukaot's transport

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

`Log.ts`,

`pino-cacache.ts`, `pino-pretty.ts` and the `pino` dependency move out of `core/blong-gogo` and into
the library, so one component owns the wire format: lukaot decides that a signal was emitted, pino
writes it, and lukaot supplies both renderings — the JSON line and the coloured human line
`semantic-log` prints today — plus the on-disk cache `blong-dev     log` reads. The framework keeps
no opinion about format, and a third-party sink is a pino transport rather than an `ILog`
implementation.

### D-906 — Payload shapes become declared captures, masked before retention

> _2026-11-19 · core/lukaot · active_

The payload-shaped sites D-904 left un-converted become **captures**: a declared identifier with a
shape, a detail rung and an optional note, rendered by a per-shape renderer and masked before
anything is retained. The design was written up beside the plan, which has since been archived; this
entry keeps the choices that the code will not show, and the issue is
[#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

A capture resolves **per adapter instance**, not per adapter type, and a shape can be switched off
on its own. The view is built when the port instance is built, from that instance's own
configuration, so an instance that turned a shape off has no member for it at all and the call chain
runs through the optional chaining without a call, a closure or a payload. That is the grain an
operator needs: capture is turned on for the one adapter being debugged, and its siblings of the
same type pay nothing.

Masking reuses `redact.ts`'s path language and, more importantly, its position before every sink, so
a withheld value is absent from the ring buffer and the retained store rather than only from output.
It gains partial and hash modes, case-insensitive header names and byte ranges for fixed-offset
frames; a shape ships a floor of rules and a scope may only add to it, never remove it.

The payload is never constructed for a call that will not record. The slot is absent per instance
and per shape (D-893), and the payload itself rides a thunk that the policy decides whether to
invoke — which is what lets a selector target one method of one adapter without paying for the
packet at the other call sites of the same port.

A capture earns its own entry in the store instead of folding into a shape, because a captured
payload is one-of-a-kind and the store's denoise would otherwise keep the newest one and a count.
Over the 1024 byte threshold its bulk rides the existing payload reference.

Error objects are not captures — a failure is already a signal (D-890) — but they showed what the
vocabulary must support for them: **one declared identifier per case**, not a shared fallback. The
seven `warn(error)` sites are seven different failures, and silencing one of them must not silence
the others.

### D-1041 — A trace and a parent resolve to what the local store retained, not a replay

> _2026-11-28 · core/lukaot · active_

The printed reference group carries four linkable members and one label: record, template, trace,
payload, and the parent id after `p=`. Record, template and payload resolve against the local
`cacache` store, so the editor answers them with one key lookup. A trace and a parent cannot: the
local store keeps one entry per shape plus the per-emit records whose fold would hide something, and
a trace is an index the service keeps over what it ingested, so no local key carries it. Rather than
stop printing the trace, the editor resolves it by scanning the store for the records that carry
that trace id, and says in the document that the listing is what was retained locally rather than a
replay of the request. The same answer is available to an agent as `blong-dev log --trace-id <id>`.
A parent id is linked the same way and commonly reports "not retained", which is the honest answer:
the record it names exists only if its own fold could not stand for it.
